passage:
Lucia stood at the door of the art room with her portfolio pressed to her chest, ready to be told the club was full. She had moved to the town in September, spoke slowly in the new language, and had eaten lunch alone for three weeks.
Ms. Esther glanced up from sorting brushes. "You must be Lucia. There's a stool by the window, and the kettle is on if you want tea."
Nobody asked where she was from or why she talked that way. Lucia sat down, and her shoulders dropped for the first time in weeks. When the bell rang she stayed to wash the brushes.
"Same time Thursday?" Ms. Esther said.
Lucia nodded. Walking out, she decided that next month she would save a stool for whoever came in next.

qa.q: Where did Lucia sit in the art room?
qa.a: She sat on the stool by the window.

qa.q: What was Lucia feeling when her shoulders dropped?
qa.a: She felt relief: she had expected to be turned away, and the easy welcome without questions let her relax at last. 😊

qa.q: How could Lucia hold on to this kindness?
qa.a: She can keep the Thursday club as an anchor, and later, as she plans, save a stool for the next newcomer.

qa.q: How might Ms. Esther see what happened at the door?
qa.a: To Ms. Esther it may have been an ordinary welcome to a new student, though it meant far more to Lucia after weeks of eating alone.

grounding: A teacher welcomes a newcomer without judgment, she feels deep relief, and she resolves to pay the kindness forward.

passage: Pankaj had been dreading his first week at Sunrise Public School in Andheri. He was repeating Class 10, a year older than everyone, and he'd heard the whispers in the corridor: 'That's the one who failed.' On Thursday he hovered at the door of the robotics lab. Gopika Ma'am looked up from a tangle of wires. 'Pankaj, right? Good, I need someone with steady hands. Can you solder?' Nobody asked about last year. By five o'clock he'd fixed a motor and laughed twice. On the bus home he leaned his head against the window and felt his shoulders drop for the first time in months. Three weeks later, a thin new boy stood frozen at the same lab door, clutching his bag. Pankaj waved him in. 'Come, we need steady hands.'

qa.q: What did Gopika Ma'am ask Pankaj at the lab door?
qa.a: Whether he could solder, because she needed someone with steady hands.

qa.q: What does Pankaj's dropping shoulders on the bus suggest?
qa.a: It suggests deep relief after months of tension about being judged for repeating a year 🙂

qa.q: How did Pankaj pay the kindness forward?
qa.a: He waved in a frozen new boy using the same welcoming words he had heard.

qa.q: How does Gopika Ma'am see Pankaj when he arrives?
qa.a: She sees a useful new pair of hands, not the student who failed, and welcomes him without questions.

grounding: Shows a teen repeating a year who is welcomed without judgment by a club teacher, feels relief and passes on the welcome.

passage:
'I... I wanted to try for the p-play,' Bhupen said, eyes on the floor of the hall.
'Great. Take a script,' said Charu, the drama club captain, sliding one across the stage.
'You heard me, right? I st-stammer.'
'I heard. Page four. Read the grandfather. He's grumpy, you'll love him.'
Bhupen read. It took a while. Nobody giggled. When he finished, Charu clapped once. 'You pause before the angry lines. That's actually perfect for him.'
'You're not just being nice?'
'I'm the captain. I'm never just nice. Ask anyone.'
Somebody at the back laughed. 'She's really not.'
Bhupen laughed too, and something in his chest unknotted.
'Rehearsals are Tuesday and Friday,' Charu said. 'And stay back next week? Help me with the new kids' auditions.'
'Me?'
'You know exactly how scary that door is.'

qa.q: Which part did Charu ask Bhupen to read?
How did Bhupen feel after nobody giggled at his reading?
qa.a: He felt deep relief, as something in his chest unknotted and he laughed along.

qa.q: Why is Charu's request about auditions a good idea?
qa.a: It lets Bhupen pay the welcome forward to new kids, since he knows how scary that door is.

qa.q: How does Charu see Bhupen's stammer?
qa.a: She sees it as no barrier, even noticing his pauses suit the grumpy grandfather.

grounding: Shows a teen who stammers being welcomed by a drama club without judgment, feeling relief and being invited to welcome others.
